work_packages.name: A rule asks whether two 3D shapes touch, where a ray meets one and where a moving one is stopped, and gets the same answer on the Mac, in Chrome and on the iPhone simulator
work_packages.quality_bar: Shape tests as dependable as Jolt's and Parry's at touching, grazing and degenerate cases, and the same bits on every device, as Box2D 3.1 holds its results across platforms.

items.statement: Built first, because the other items test against the contact tolerance it sets. (1) The crate states the query domain's bound, 32,768 units, and the contact tolerance, a power of two at most 1/64 of a unit, as public constants. (2) A sphere, a capsule, a cuboid and a triangle placed at each corner of the query domain, each as large as the domain allows, give finite answers from the distance, overlap, depth, ray and sweep tests. (3) Each of those tests refuses, with a typed error that names what was wrong: a shape with a coordinate beyond the bound; a non-finite coordinate; a negative radius; a motion that ends outside the domain; and a sweep asked to stop within half the tolerance over a motion longer than 4,096 units. Guard: CPU tests, in `./dev check`.

Distance and overlap. For the six pairs among sphere, capsule and cuboid and for each of the three against a triangle, the distance and the overlap test give answers written out by hand, at: apart by more than the contact tolerance; crossing by more than the tolerance; one wholly inside the other, for the pairs where one can be; and touching, set up for each pair with every closest point at a coordinate the profile holds exactly, which is an overlap at distance zero. The same with a sphere of zero radius, a capsule of zero length, a flat cuboid, a cuboid turned so that no half-edge lies along an axis, and a triangle whose corners lie on one line. In every case the overlap test is true exactly where the distance is zero. Every case is asserted at the origin and at a corner of the query domain, and with the two shapes given in either order. Guard: CPU tests, in `./dev check`.

Rays. A ray against a sphere, a capsule, a cuboid, a turned cuboid and a triangle gives the hand-worked fraction, point and normal for: a hit from outside; a start inside a sphere, a capsule or a cuboid, which is a hit at fraction zero with the normal of the shallowest way out; a ray that stops short of the shape; one that points away from it; one that passes beside it; a ray of zero length, inside a shape and outside it; a triangle met from each side, with the normal toward the ray's start each time; and a triangle met edge-on and a triangle of no area, which are misses. Each normal's length is within 2⁻²⁰ of one. Every case is asserted at the origin and at a corner of the query domain. Guard: CPU tests, in `./dev check`.

Sweeps that meet a thing on the way, for a sphere, a capsule and a cuboid moved against each of the three and against a triangle: twelve pairs, each asked to stop within the contact tolerance and within half of it. Every case begins more than the tolerance clear of what it is swept against. The hand-worked cases are, for every pair: head-on, where the motion runs along the normal of first contact; onto a face at a slant; passing by, where the path stays twice the tolerance clear; and leading away. And for the pairs that have them: head-on onto an edge and onto a corner of a cuboid and of a triangle; a triangle met from each side; and right through and out of the far side, by a sphere through a cuboid thicker than the sphere, and by a motion 10,000 times the mover's size through a triangle and through a flat cuboid. Each case that meets has the fraction and the normal of first contact written out by hand, and the point of first contact too where the two first meet at a single point. Below, the mover's place is its start plus the motion times the fraction, and the gap is what the distance test gives between the mover at its place and what it struck. (1) Passing by and leading away report nothing, and every other case reports a hit. (2) At a hit the mover at its place does not overlap what it struck, and the gap is no more than the gap asked for. (3) The fraction is not past the hand-worked fraction of first contact by more than 2⁻²⁰, so a place on the far side of what was struck fails. (4) The depth is exactly zero, and the normal's length is within 2⁻²⁰ of one. (5) The normal points out of what was struck, toward the mover: its dot product with the hand-worked normal is at least ¾ in every case, and each of its components is within 2⁻¹⁰ of the hand-worked normal in the head-on cases and in the slanted cases onto a flat face of a cuboid or of a triangle. (6) The point is on the surface of what was struck, at a place nearest the mover. The distance test between the point, taken as a sphere of no radius, and what was struck gives no more than the contact tolerance; and between the point and the mover at its place it gives no more than the gap plus the contact tolerance. So a point a unit inside a broad face fails, and any point of a patch of a face that is equally near the mover passes. Where the case has a hand-worked point, the reported point is also within the contact tolerance of it. Every case is asserted at the origin and at a corner of the query domain. Guard: CPU tests, in `./dev check`.

The crate computes with the profile's numbers and nothing else. It is registered as a rule package, so the profile's check holds it and its tests to the profile's lints, with none suppressed, on native, Wasm and simulator builds, in development and release: six passing rows that name `thrum-sim3d`. Guard: the profile's check, in `./dev check`.
items.check: python3 scripts/sim2d_profile.py check --output tmp/sim3d/profile-check.json && python3 -c "import json; rows = [r for r in json.load(open('tmp/sim3d/profile-check.json'))['rows'] if r['package'] == 'thrum-sim3d']; assert len(rows) == 6 and all(r['result'] == 'pass' for r in rows), rows"

items.statement: On the Mac, in a release build and a development build, every retained vector is reproduced bit for bit. The retained vectors are test data: every bit of the answer of each case of WP1.2, WP1.3, WP1.4, WP1.10 and WP1.11, at the origin and at a corner of the query domain, and of 1,000 seeded cases of each of the five tests, drawn across the query domain with the profile's keyed random function. The same run with one retained value changed fails and names the vector. Guard: the native comparison is a CPU test in `./dev check`.
items.check: cargo test --locked --offline -p sim3d-run --test it vectors:: && python3 scripts/sim3d_conformance.py vectors --target mac-metal

items.statement: As Wasm in Chrome, every retained vector of WP1.6 is reproduced bit for bit. The conformance command takes Chrome's lock itself around its browser run, so the item names none. Record: the Chrome arm of the three-target run.

In the iPhone simulator, every retained vector of WP1.6 is reproduced bit for bit. Function only. The conformance command takes the simulator for its turn itself, so the item names no lock. Record: the simulator arm of the three-target run.

The tests are proved by answers that do not come from themselves, the contact tolerance was set from a measurement, a sweep reports no place it has not tested, and what was translated from elsewhere is on record.
items.ask: 1. Are the expected answers in the distance, overlap, depth, ray and sweep tests written out from geometry, with coordinates the profile holds exactly, and not computed by the functions under test? 2. Does each test's answer depend on its arguments alone: is there no cache, counter or other state that outlives a call? 3. Does each test subtract one reference point from the coordinates it reads before it multiplies, so that a case at a corner of the query domain is computed in a local frame? 4. Does the work package's evidence hold a record, made before the contact tolerance was fixed, of the gap left at the reported place by every sweep case of WP1.4 at the origin and at the corners of the query domain, and by a sweep from one corner of the domain to the opposite one? Is the largest gap recorded for the sweeps asked to stop within the tolerance no more than the tolerance, and for those asked to stop within half of it no more than half? 5. Does a sweep report a hit met on the way only after testing the reported place, with the mover there clear of what it struck and within the gap asked for? When its fixed number of steps runs out, does it go on by halving to such a hit or to a miss, and never report the place it had reached untested? 6. Does `docs/provenance/SIM-3D.md` list every file translated or adapted from another project with its source, revision and licence, or say that none was, and is none GPL or share-alike?

items.statement: Depth, and sweeps that begin in contact. (1) The depth test gives the hand-worked depth, to within 2⁻¹⁶ of a unit, and the hand-worked normal of the shallowest way out, each component to within 2⁻¹⁰, in cases each set up so that one way out is the shallowest: two shapes whose hulls are apart and whose radii cross, among them two unit spheres with centres one unit apart along an axis, whose depth is exactly one along that axis; two whose hulls cross, namely a cuboid in a cuboid, a capsule through a cuboid, a sphere whose centre is inside a cuboid, a sphere of no radius inside a cuboid, and a capsule and a cuboid through a triangle; and one shape wholly inside another. For two shapes that do not overlap it gives zero. (2) Where the two hulls lie in one plane, along one line or at one point, several ways out are equally shallow. The cases are: a capsule lying in the plane of a flat cuboid, inside its outline; a unit sphere centred at the origin with a capsule of radius one whose ends are (−2, 0, 0) and (2, 0, 0), the same with the capsule along y and along z, and with its ends at (−3, −4, 0) and (3, 4, 0); two capsules whose lines overlap along one line; and two unit spheres at one place. In each the depth is the two radii added, exactly, and the normal's length is within 2⁻²⁰ of one. The normal's dot product with each direction the two hulls lie along, which is the flat cuboid's two edges or the capsule's line, is within 2⁻¹⁰ of zero, so a normal along a capsule's line fails however the capsule is turned. For the two spheres at one place, the mover moved half a unit along the reported normal, and moved half a unit against it, stands 1½ deep each time, to within 2⁻¹⁶: a motion against a tie's normal does not lead deeper. (3) In every overlapping case of (1) and (2) the mover, set at its place plus the normal times the depth, touches what it struck: the distance test and the depth test there each give no more than the contact tolerance. (4) A sweep of each of those cases whose depth is more than the tolerance reports fraction zero with that depth and that normal, for a motion that leads in, one that leads along, one that leads away and one of no length. (5) For each of the twelve pairs of WP1.4, a sweep that begins half the gap asked for clear of what it is swept against, and one that begins overlapping it by half the tolerance, each report fraction zero, a depth of exactly zero and the hand-worked normal, for the same four motions. (6) A sweep that begins twice the tolerance clear reports nothing where its motion leads along, leads away or has no length. Every case is asserted at the origin and at a corner of the query domain, and every sweep is asked to stop within the tolerance and within half of it. Guard: CPU tests, in `./dev check`.

Two shapes that both move, each case asked to stop within the contact tolerance. The hand-worked cases are: head-on at unequal speeds, with spheres of radius ½ at x = 0 and x = 4 that move by +6 and −2, which first touch at fraction ⅜ with the struck sphere's surface at x = 2¾; one shape overtaking another along one line; two spheres on paths at right angles that reach one point half-way through, where neither begins or ends within the box the other sweeps; a capsule and a cuboid closing at a slant; two moving apart; and two a unit apart moving by the same motion. Each case that meets has the fraction and the normal of first contact written out by hand. Below, each shape's place is its own start plus its own motion times the fraction, and the gap is what the distance test gives between the two shapes at their places. (1) The last two cases report nothing, and the others report a hit. (2) At a hit the mover at its place does not overlap the struck shape at its place, and the gap is no more than the tolerance. (3) The fraction is not past the hand-worked fraction of first contact by more than 2⁻²⁰. (4) The depth is exactly zero, and the normal's dot product with the hand-worked normal is at least ¾. (5) The point is on the surface of the struck shape at its place, at a place nearest the mover at its place. The distance test between the point, taken as a sphere of no radius, and the struck shape at its place gives no more than the tolerance; and between the point and the mover at its place it gives no more than the gap plus the tolerance. So a point inside the struck shape fails, and so does a point on the struck shape where it stood as the motion began. In the head-on case the point is within the tolerance of (2¾, 0, 0), and so not at the 3½ where the struck sphere's surface would be had it stood still. Every case is asserted at the origin and at a corner of the query domain. Guard: CPU tests, in `./dev check`.

work_packages.name: A rule finds what is near a point, along a ray and in a moving shape's path among 10,000 colliders, and every answer matches a brute-force search
work_packages.quality_bar: Queries as dependable as Jolt's and Unity Physics' world queries: the right colliders, every time, in an order a game can rely on, with whatever a warmed build or query allocates on record.

items.statement: For an overlap with a sphere, a capsule and a cuboid, the nearest k to a point within a distance, a ray, and a sweep of each of the three shapes, the index gives exactly the sequence a brute-force search over the same colliders gives with the same pair tests, sorted by the design's order. A ray is asked for every answer and for the first alone. A sweep is asked for every answer, for the first alone, and for the first met on the way with every contact there from the start, and is asked to stop within the contact tolerance and within half of it. The scenes are: an empty index; one collider; two that coincide; 500 colliders spread so that few touch, 500 packed so that each touches several, 500 at one point, and 500 mixed in kind and in size from a point to larger than the whole crowd, each of those four at the origin and at a corner of the query domain; colliders that exactly touch the query shape, at the origin and at a corner of the query domain; a query wider than every collider together; a query with one slot left out; and 10,000 colliders packed three deep, for four queries of each kind. Guard: CPU tests, each inside the merge tier's ten seconds, in `./dev check`.
items.ask: Does the brute-force side visit every collider without using the index's tree or its boxes, and sort by the design's key? Is each scene in the statement generated, with its colliders drawn from the profile's keyed random function?

items.statement: The order of answers is the design's, in hand-worked cases: an overlap and the nearest k come nearest centre first, and colliders at one distance in ascending slot; a ray and a sweep come earliest first, and colliders at one fraction in ascending slot; the nearest k among more than k colliders at one distance are the k lowest slots; the first hit asked for alone is the first of every hit; and a sweep asked for the first met on the way gives every contact there from the start, in ascending slot, and then the first of the hits that follow them. Guard: CPU tests, in `./dev check`.

The index at the edge of the query domain. (1) A build is refused, with an error that names the slot, for a collider with a point outside the query domain, for a non-finite coordinate or a negative radius, and for slots that do not ascend; after a refused build the index holds what it held and gives the answers it gave. A query with a point outside the domain is refused with an error that names it. (2) A collider and a query that reach a face of the domain and do not pass it are admitted. The cases, each as a collider in a build and as the shape of an overlap query, are: a sphere of radius ½ centred at (32,767½, 0, 0); a cuboid with a face on x = 32,768; and the path box of that sphere moved by (0, 8, 0) along the face, which is the box of every place it stood, widened by the contact tolerance on every side and then cut back to the domain, so that it ends at x = 32,768. (3) Two spheres of radius ½ that touch on the domain's face, centred at (32,767½, 0, 0) and (32,767½, 1, 0), are given to an index as their path boxes, made as in (2). An overlap query with either's path box finds the other's. (4) An index whose colliders stand against the faces and in a corner of the domain, those of (2) among them, answers an overlap, a ray and a sweep as the brute-force search of WP2.1 does. Guard: CPU tests, in `./dev check`.

An index built from a list gives the answers a new index built from that list gives, whatever it held before: after a build from another list, and after a build of 10,000 colliders followed by one of three. Its queries take the index by shared reference, and a compile-time test shows its type can be shared between threads. Guard: CPU tests, in `./dev check`.

The index keeps its storage between builds, and a query writes into storage its caller keeps. The allocations made by a warmed build and by a warmed query of each kind at 10,000 colliders are counted on the Mac and printed by name: a build, an overlap with each of the three shapes, the nearest k, a ray and a sweep. The counts are observations: the test fails only when one is missing, and the log explains any that is not zero. Guard: the counting test stays in the tree as its own test binary and runs in `./dev check`.

The retained vectors gain the index's cases: the answers, as slots in order with every bit of each fraction, point, normal and depth, of each query kind of WP2.1 on its 500-collider mixed scene, at the origin and at a corner of the query domain. Among the sweeps is one that begins inside a collider, deeper than the contact tolerance, so a depth that is not zero is among the retained answers. On the Mac they are reproduced bit for bit in a release build and a development build, with WP1's vectors unchanged. Guard: the native comparison is a CPU test in `./dev check`.
items.check: cargo test --locked --offline -p sim3d-run --test it vectors:: && python3 scripts/sim3d_conformance.py vectors --target mac-metal

items.statement: As Wasm in Chrome, where a machine word is 32 bits, every retained vector is reproduced bit for bit, the index's cases among them. The conformance command takes Chrome's lock itself, so the item names none. The simulator's arm waits for the module's last work package: it shares the Mac's processor and word size, so here it could show nothing the Mac did not. Record: the Chrome arm of the conformance run.
The index's answers do not depend on how its tree was built, and its two counts are honest.
items.ask: 1. Is the order of every answer fixed by the design's key alone, whether by sorting the answers on it or, where only the first is asked for, by keeping the least key among the candidates visited, so that no answer would change if the tree were built another way? 2. Is each pair test called with the shapes and the whole motion as given, also when only the first hit is asked for, so that its answer cannot depend on what else was found? 3. Are the tree's boxes widened by more than the contact tolerance, and do the exactly-touching scenes of WP2.1 exercise that? 4. Does a build reuse the index's storage by design, and does a query take its scratch from its caller? 5. Is the tree a function of the list alone: does its build use no `usize` or pointer value as a key, and nothing left from an earlier build? 6. Is the count of boxes examined raised wherever a box of the tree is tested against a query, an inner box or a leaf's, and the count of pair tests wherever a pair test is called, so that no query can look at a box or test a pair without counting it? Are both counts returned with the answers and kept nowhere after the call?

items.statement: The tree narrows, by the two counts a query gives with its answers: the pair tests it made, and the boxes of the tree it examined, inner boxes and leaves alike. The scene is 10,000 spheres of radius ½ whose centres stand 4 units apart on a grid of 10 by 10 by 100. Six questions are each asked from four places inside the grid: an overlap with a sphere of radius 1; the nearest 4 within 6 units; a ray 8 units long, for every answer and for the first alone; and a sweep of a sphere of radius ½ over 8 units, for every answer and for the first alone. Each gives the sequence the brute-force search of WP2.1 gives, makes no more than 100 pair tests, and examines no more than 1,000 boxes. A traversal that looks at every leaf's box examines 10,000 or more, and fails. Guard: CPU tests, in `./dev check`.
